title: Module quiz: Scenario: code generation with Claude Code

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. A rule file for the handlers lists `paths: src/api`, and the audit says that it matches none of the project's files. What is the likely cause?

options.text: Rule files are read only when a session is first started
options.says: Ruled out because path-scoped rules load when a matching file is read: "A rule with a `paths` list loads when Claude works with a file that matches one of its globs".

options.text: The entry is a bare folder name and not a glob that ends in a double star
options.says: A bare folder name is not a glob: "write a folder as `src/api/**`".

options.text: Handlers are covered by the command folder, which takes priority in every session
options.says: Ruled out because the command folder holds commands and not conventions: "A command file in the project, `.claude/commands/review.md`, committed to the repository".

options.text: The path needs the word handlers in it for the rule to be found
options.says: Ruled out because the match is by glob on file paths and not by a word: "`**` crosses folders and `*` stays inside one".

questions.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. Three specs of the flawed project get no conventions at all. What closes the gap?

options.text: A testing rule whose glob, such as `**/*.test.tsx`, reaches test files in any folder
options.says: A rule with a glob reaches test files wherever they sit: "`**/*.test.tsx` reaches test files in any folder".

options.text: A longer root file that names each test file under a heading of its own
options.says: Ruled out because the root file leaves the choice to the model: "One root file with a section per area leaves Claude to infer which section applies".

options.text: A skill for tests that each developer starts by hand before a commit
options.says: Ruled out because a path starts no skill: "a skill is invoked, or chosen by the model from its description, and a path match does not start it".

options.text: A memory file placed in the one folder that holds most of the tests
options.says: Ruled out because a folder file does not reach the others: "each file is bound to its directory, and test files next to their sources are in all of them".

questions.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. In the example's fixed project, `docs/readme.md` is opened. Which conventions load for it?

options.text: Only the root file's, since no rule has a glob that matches it
options.says: The output shows `docs/readme.md <- CLAUDE.md only`: no rule reaches it, and the root file loads in every session.

options.text: The testing rule as well, since a readme is also a kind of test
options.says: Ruled out because the testing rule has globs for test files: "`**/*.test.tsx` reaches test files in any folder".

options.text: The components rule, as the nearest rule by folder
options.says: Ruled out because a match is by glob and not by nearness: "`**` crosses folders and `*` stays inside one".

options.text: None at all, since the root file loads only for source files
options.says: Ruled out because the root file is not conditional: "The root `CLAUDE.md` and the rule files without a `paths` list load at the start of every session".

questions.stem: Scenario S2, a team using Claude Code on a shared codebase. The audit of the flawed project prints `env-readable`. What removes that finding?

options.text: A rule file whose glob matches `.env`
options.says: Ruled out because a rule loads conventions and denies nothing: "A rule with a `paths` list loads when Claude works with a file that matches one of its globs".

options.text: A line in the root file that asks Claude not to read `.env`
options.says: Ruled out because a sentence in a file is a request: "a sentence in a memory file is a request that the model weighs".

options.text: A deny rule for reading `.env` in the settings
options.says: The finding says that the settings do not deny the file: "`env-readable` and `bare-bash-allowed`: the settings do not deny reading `.env`, or allow the whole Bash tool."

options.text: A review command with a read-only list of tools
options.says: Ruled out because the command's tools are another matter: "a shared review command with a description and read-only tools".

origin.section: The audit: a checklist that reads the files
